notes: Every question was written for this assignment, not copied from a paper's own evaluation.
required_all is a list of groups. Every group must match at least one alternative for an answer to be graded 'correct'.
The facts in required_all were checked by reading the indexed PDF text; the notes field records the location.
Unanswerable questions are graded 'refused_correctly' only when the assistant refuses; a confident invented answer is 'wrong'.

questions.question: What BLEU score did the Transformer achieve on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task?
questions.notes: Abstract and Section 6.1 (p. 1, p. 8).

questions.question: How long did the big Transformer model train, and on how many GPUs?
questions.notes: Section 5.2 and Section 6.1 (p. 7, p. 8): 300,000 steps, 3.5 days, 8 P100 GPUs.

questions.question: Why does scaled dot-product attention divide the dot products by the square root of d_k?
questions.notes: Section 3.2.1 (p. 4): large dot products push softmax into regions with extremely small gradients.

questions.question: What are the three ways multi-head attention is used inside the Transformer?
questions.notes: Section 3.2.3 (p. 5): encoder-decoder attention, encoder self-attention, masked decoder self-attention.

questions.question: How many identical layers are in the encoder and decoder of the base Transformer?
questions.notes: Section 3.1 (p. 3): N = 6 in both stacks.

questions.question: Which optimizer trained the Transformer, and how many warmup steps did it use?
questions.notes: Section 5.3 (p. 7): Adam with warmup_steps = 4000.

questions.question: Why is masking used in the decoder's self-attention layers?
questions.notes: Section 3.1 and 3.2.3 (p. 3, p. 5): prevents attending to later positions.

questions.question: Which mathematical functions does the Transformer use for positional encodings?
questions.notes: Section 3.5 (p. 6): sine and cosine functions of different frequencies.

questions.question: How does Moshi model spoken dialogue, and what kind of conversation does that enable?
questions.notes: Abstract and Section 3.1 (p. 1, p. 6).

questions.question: What is Mimi, and what role does it play in Moshi?
questions.notes: Section 3.3 (p. 9): Mimi is a neural audio codec that turns audio into discrete tokens and back.

questions.question: What is the Inner Monologue method in Moshi, and what does it improve?
questions.notes: Abstract and Section 3.4.4: predicts time-aligned text tokens before audio tokens; improves linguistic quality and factuality.

questions.question: What are the two Transformer models inside the RQ-Transformer, and what does each do?
questions.notes: Section 3.4.1 (p. 13): a temporal Transformer over timesteps and a depth Transformer over codebook steps.

questions.question: How large is the unsupervised audio dataset used to train Moshi?
questions.notes: Section 4.2 (p. 17): 7 million hours.

questions.question: What latency does Moshi report for full-duplex spoken dialogue?
questions.notes: Abstract (p. 1): theoretical 160 ms, 200 ms in practice.

questions.question: What is dynamic chunking, and what does it replace in the H-Net?
questions.notes: Abstract (p. 1): replaces the tokenization-LM-detokenization pipeline with a single end-to-end model.

questions.question: How does the routing module decide where a chunk boundary should be?
questions.notes: Section 2.2.1 (p. 6): cosine similarity between adjacent encoder outputs gives a boundary probability.

questions.question: What does the dechunking layer do in an H-Net?
questions.notes: Section 2.2.2 (p. 6): a smoothing module and an upsampler restore the original resolution.

questions.question: How does a byte-level H-Net with one stage of dynamic chunking compare with a BPE-tokenized Transformer?
questions.notes: Section 1 (p. 3): matches perplexity and downstream performance at sizes exceeding 1B parameters.

questions.question: What problem with fixed-vocabulary tokenization motivates the Dynamic Chunking paper?
questions.notes: Abstract and Section 1 (p. 1): tokenization is a handcrafted preprocessing barrier to end-to-end models.

questions.question: What is the capital of France?
questions.notes: Out-of-scope control. The scope filter should refuse before any model call.

questions.question: Does the Moshi paper report results on video understanding benchmarks?
questions.notes: Control for an in-domain-sounding but absent topic. The paper is about speech, not video.

questions.question: What learning rate did the Dynamic Chunking paper use for ImageNet classification?
questions.notes: ImageNet appears only in a reference title; the paper does not report ImageNet experiments.

questions.question: How does the Transformer paper handle speech input?
questions.notes: Attention Is All You Need studies translation and parsing, not speech input.
